questions.text: Your jurisdiction uses an AI tool to monitor contract compliance and match invoices to contract terms. The system suddenly flags a vendor that has had a clean record for two years as having multiple discrepancies. What is the most appropriate response?

answers.text: Accept the AI's assessment and immediately issue a notice of non-compliance to the vendor
Dismiss the flags since the vendor has a strong track record and the AI may be malfunctioning
Investigate the flagged discrepancies using the underlying contract documents and invoice records before taking any action
Switch to a different AI tool to see if it produces the same result

questions.text: A staff member wants to use a free AI tool they found online to analyze a contract containing sensitive vendor pricing data. What should they do first?

answers.text: Proceed, since the tool produces accurate results in their testing
Ask a colleague to review the output to catch any errors
Use the tool but remove the vendor names before uploading
Check whether the tool is on their jurisdiction's approved list and complies with data security requirements

questions.text: A jurisdiction is rolling out a new AI tool and several staff members have expressed concerns about job displacement. Which of the following are appropriate responses from procurement leadership? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Reassure staff that their concerns are unfounded and move forward without addressing them further
Communicate clearly and early about what the tool is, what it isn't, and what problems it aims to solve
Pause the rollout indefinitely until all staff concerns are fully resolved
Provide structured training and ongoing learning resources so staff feel confident using the tool
Limit access to the tool to staff who are already comfortable with AI
Create space for staff to raise concerns and give feedback throughout the rollout
Emphasize that AI will handle repetitive tasks, freeing staff to focus on higher-value work that requires their expertise

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the goal of cross-functional collaboration in AI risk management?

answers.text: To slow down AI adoption until all risks are fully understood
To transfer responsibility for AI risk from procurement to IT
To bring procurement, IT, legal, and leadership together to assess risks and define mitigation strategies before deployment
To create a committee that approves every AI output before it is used
